item.title: Eighteen launches, no program names: a call for disclosure
item.description: On the evening of October 15, a Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg carrying a classified payload for the Space Force. The booster, B1081, came back to the droneship on its 28th flight. SpaceX ended the broadcast at stage separation, as it does. The payload was not described, the satellites were not counted and no program was named.

item.title: Satellite on orbit responded to voice command in experimental first
item.description: Operators on the ground successfully directed a satellite on orbit with a voice command for the first time. Researchers told SpaceNews that their experimental success could be a step toward a future in which responsive satellites can listen for distress calls and emergency signals from ships at sea.

item.title: Space is a warfighting domain. Our industrial base must reflect that.
item.description: When I served as acting Secretary of Defense, I took a trip to Buckley Space Force Base. I went as someone who understood in the abstract that space had become contested. I left understanding it in my gut. Watching the men and women who track every object on orbit and leverage space-based sensors to spot a launch anywhere on Earth to give our ground forces the seconds of warning that save lives, I came away with a conviction that has only deepened since: Space is a warfighting domain, and we are not yet organized to win in it.
